The dearth of reliable quantitative data on the probable effects of various types of conservation, peakload procing, and land management negates the value of such measures as alternatives to the construction of major projects. The lead time required for the licensing and construction of such projects precludes waiting for the results of studies which are now in progress, and which may, in the future, provide the necessary quantitative data.
The Procus Production Cost Computer Program used to compute the estimated production costs shown in Table 8-2 does not ignore the possibility (and probability) that portions of the pumping energy will be derived from fossilfueled base-load plants.
